# soc-evals

Score a managed SOC proposal against the five questions that decide whether it works.

## What it does

Evaluates a SOC-as-a-Service proposal across five dimensions:
- Telemetry coverage (percent of estate instrumented)
- Escalation SLA (minutes to human acknowledging)
- Data location (in-country, offshore, unknown)
- Response authority (none, limited, full)
- Tuning ownership (vendor, customer, shared)
- Cadence (monthly, quarterly, never)

Outputs a verdict: BUY, CONDITIONAL, or REJECT.

## Key files

- soc_evals.py: main CLI tool (argparse)
- test_soc_evals.py: 11 tests

## CLI usage

    python soc_evals.py [--coverage 85] [--sla 15] [--data in-country] [--authority full] [--tuning shared] [--cadence quarterly] [--json] [--report]

## Flags

- --coverage: percent of estate instrumented (default: 85)
- --sla: escalation minutes to human acknowledging (default: 15)
- --data: data location (in-country, offshore, unknown)
- --authority: response authority (none, limited, full)
- --tuning: tuning ownership (vendor, customer, shared)
- --cadence: tuning cadence (monthly, quarterly, never)
- --json: machine-readable output
- --report: one paste-ready summary line

## Exit codes

- 0: verdict is BUY or CONDITIONAL
- 1: verdict is REJECT

## Design patterns

- Zero dependencies (stdlib only)
- Single file (soc_evals.py)
- MIT license
- --report mode for paste-ready output
- Exit code 0/1 for CI integration
